title: Ops daily standup - 2026-07-31
transcript:
Ravi Patel: Okay, let's get started, it's four o'clock on a Friday so I'll keep this tight. Agenda is recon breaks from today's end-of-day, the wire queue, a payments item on the counterparty side, and month-end prep since tomorrow rolls into August. Tasha, you first.
Tasha Greene: Sure. ReconLegacy finished the batch at about 3:40, which is a bit later than usual. We have 14 open breaks coming out of it, down from 22 yesterday. Nine of those are timing breaks between SettlementEngine and GLCore that I expect to clear on the Monday run. Three are fee accrual mismatches, and two I can't explain yet.
Ravi Patel: What's the two you can't explain?
Tasha Greene: Both are brokerage cash movements. One is tied to {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00237}}, where the GL shows a debit that SettlementEngine doesn't have a matching settlement for. The other is on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00455}}, a small variance, about $412, looks like a rounding or FX conversion issue. The second one is probably nothing, the first one I'm more worried about.
Ravi Patel: How big is the first one?
Tasha Greene: $48,500. It's been aging since Wednesday. I pinged the RM on that account, Linda Barnes, to see if the client had initiated anything off-platform, but nothing back yet.
Ravi Patel: Okay. Since that account is flagged high risk on the client side, I want it documented properly. Tasha, put the break details in the #recon thread and loop in Compliance if it's still open Monday morning. Don't wait longer than that.
Tasha Greene: Will do. I'll also attach the GL journal reference so nobody has to hunt for it.
Ravi Patel: Good. Mike, wire room?
Mike Herrera: Yeah, queue is clean right now. We processed 63 outbound wires today, total around $11.2 million. Two were held for callback verification, one released already, the other is still waiting on the client to pick up. That's the one tied to {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0111}}. We tried the number on file, {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0111}}, twice, and it went to voicemail.
Ravi Patel: Do not release without the callback. If it's not done by cutoff, it rolls to Monday. Mike, make sure the RM knows so they can try a second channel.
Mike Herrera: Understood. I'll email Linda Barnes and note it in the WireRoom console. I won't use the email on file to confirm anything, callback only on the verified number.
Derrick Anderson: Just to add on wires, we had a brief slowdown around 1:15 where PaymentsGateway was responding slow. Took about six, seven minutes per submission instead of a few seconds. It cleared on its own, but I want to flag it in case it ties to FraudScore latency.
Craig Garner: Yeah, I saw that too from the payments side. My ACH batch was delayed about ten minutes. I looked at it, and FraudScore was the bottleneck. It depends on DataLake and there was a heavy query running on it during that window, from what I could tell.
Ravi Patel: That would make sense. Craig, did you open a ticket?
Craig Garner: Not yet. I'll open one today and tag Technology, specifically Omar or Barbara on the SRE side, so they can check the DataLake load around that time.
Ravi Patel: Good. Make sure the ticket includes timestamps, Derrick can give you the ones from the wire queue.
Derrick Anderson: Yep, I'll send them right after this. First slow submission was 1:14, last one was around 1:22.
Ravi Patel: Craig, anything else on payments?
Craig Garner: One item. We have an incoming ACH return from the counterparty Giles, Johnson and Adams, and the beneficiary details on their side look off. The settlement instruction on file for them, {{CP_ACCOUNT:cp_040}}, hasn't been updated since last year, and they sent a notice that it may have changed. I don't want to send anything further until we confirm.
Ravi Patel: Agreed. Don't update anything off an emailed notice. Verify through the contact we have on record, and get the change request in writing through the standard process. Who owns that?
Craig Garner: I'll own it. I'll call their treasury contact using the number from our records and file the change request with Compliance for sign-off.
Ravi Patel: Good. Until it's confirmed, put a hold on any outbound payments to that counterparty. Derrick and Mike, you two make sure the wire room is aware.
Derrick Anderson: Got it, I'll add a hold flag in WireRoom.
Mike Herrera: And I'll mention it at the Monday handoff so nobody releases by mistake.
Ravi Patel: Okay. Month-end. Tomorrow is Saturday but the month-end close runs through Monday. Tasha, what do you need?
Tasha Greene: I need the GLCore cutoff confirmed with Finance. If anything posts late Friday night, I'll need a second recon run before the close. I'd like Monday's batch to start at 6 a.m. rather than the usual time.
Ravi Patel: I'll ask Martin Osei's team to confirm the cutoff and I'll let you know tonight. Also, I'd like Monday's batch results by 8:30 so we have time to clear breaks.
Tasha Greene: Should be fine unless the batch runs long like today.
Ravi Patel: If it does, tell me right away and we'll escalate to Technology. ReconLegacy is on Oracle 11g and I don't want a surprise at month-end.
Mike Herrera: One more thing from me. I'm out Monday morning for a dentist appointment, so Derrick will cover the callback follow-up.
Derrick Anderson: That's fine, I'll cover.
Ravi Patel: Great. Let me recap action items. Tasha: document the $48,500 break in #recon and escalate to Compliance Monday if still open, plus request the 6 a.m. batch start. Mike: email the RM on the held wire and keep the callback-only rule. Derrick: send timestamps to Craig and add the hold flag for the counterparty. Craig: open the ticket with Technology on the slowdown and own the counterparty verification and change request. And I'll confirm the GL cutoff with Finance tonight. Anything else?
Tasha Greene: Nothing from me.
Craig Garner: All good.
Ravi Patel: Okay, thanks everyone. Have a good weekend, and please keep your phones on tomorrow in case something breaks.
